bodyEn: Chelsea thought they had little chance of signing Morgan Rogers at the start of the summer. Xabi Alonso and the club’s recruitment team had the England international as a priority target but a deal seemed unlikely. Chelsea had endured a disappointing season, missing out on European football after finishing 10th, and their expectation was that Rogers would leave Aston Villa for Arsenal.

It was towards the end of the World Cup that Chelsea were made aware of a window of opportunity. Although Arsenal could claim to be London’s top dogs after winning the Premier League they dithered in talks with Villa, raising the prospect of another club stepping in.

Mikel Arteta talked about being bold in the market after Arsenal’s defeat by Paris Saint-Germain in the Champions League final. Arteta wanted more in attack. A new option on the left was a priority; Leandro Trossard and Gabriel Martinelli were up for sale and everything pointed towards Arsenal making their move for Rogers at the end of June.

Yet the lines became blurred. Arsenal had a fee of £80m in mind, while Villa wanted more, particularly after Nottingham Forest sold Elliot Anderson to Manchester City for £116m. Time dragged on. How serious were Arsenal? There was also interest in Julián Alvarez, Vinícius Júnior and Bradley Barcola. Villa waited and the price for Rogers went up. Arsenal, beaten to the punch in the end, will have a look at what they could have won when Chelsea and Rogers visit the Emirates Stadium on Sunday.

Chelsea were decisive. They were tracking Rogers before he left Middlesbrough for Villa in February 2024. Joe Shields, one of Chelsea’s five sporting directors, worked with Rogers at Manchester City’s academy. The signing was not done on a whim. Chelsea have a good relationship with Villa’s owners and moved quickly after opening club-to-club talks a day after Rogers played in England’s World Cup semi-final defeat by Argentina. The fee was £117m and Chelsea did not struggle to convince Rogers. Alonso wooed him and the deal was confirmed five days after negotiations began.

There was no last-ditch move from Arsenal. They signed Christos Tzolis from Club Brugge for £34m two days later and focused on other targets. When the window closed, though, Arteta’s options on the left looked a little light. Martinelli and Trossard left but only Tzolis arrived. Eberechi Eze and Noni Madueke are alternatives. It is hard not to feel that Arsenal could have done with Rogers, even though Chelsea have paid a high price for him.

It remains to be seen whether the 24-year-old can prove he merits becoming the third-most expensive player in English football history. For context, the fee is the consequence of the market threatening to rise out of control and the money spent on many players starting to feel meaningless. It is worth pointing out, too, that money flowed back and forth between Chelsea and Villa all summer. Even so the price will follow Rogers around, so it is just as well he has made an excellent start.

Rogers has been involved in four of Chelsea’s seven goals in their first two league games. He scored in the 3-2 win at Fulham and later combined with João Pedro to set up Cole Palmer’s goal. He created Pedro Neto’s goal in last weekend’s 4-3 win over Brighton and played a key role when Jorrel Hato played in João Pedro to score.

Chelsea have thrilled in attack so far, João Pedro, Rogers and Palmer combining to devastating effect. Alonso, an adaptable manager, wants more control but his transitional football has been a delight. Chelsea were mannered and controlled during Enzo Maresca’s time in charge. It is felt that Alonso has recognised the Premier League’s shift towards power and athleticism. Rogers fits into the Spaniard’s system. Thomas Tuchel loves Rogers for his connectivity and pressing. It is significant that England’s energy levels rose in their quarter-final against Norway after the introduction of Rogers and Djed Spence late in the second half.

Chelsea needed more strength, more speed. Rogers, able to play anywhere in attacking midfield or as a No 8, looks a better fit in Alonso’s 3-4-2-1 than Enzo Fernández, sold this week to Manchester City for £125m. He has played with Palmer as one of the No 10s but has a responsibility to drift left, a role that is unlikely to have suited Fernández. Arsenal’s impeccable defence will be tested by Chelsea’s front three.

The Rogers-Palmer partnership has clicked. They are old friends and banter over the “ice cold” celebration. Rogers is a bubbly character and can get on with anyone. Chelsea are keen to improve the culture in the dressing room. It is felt that Alonso has shifted the mood after last year’s rebellions. The squad are united. It is one of the reasons why Chelsea decided to sell Fernández on deadline day. They did not need the headache of reintegrating the Argentinian.

This is a fresh start. The signing of Rogers, who was the Professional Footballers’ Association’s young player of the year in 2025, was a sign of Chelsea’s intent. Rogers was one of the best players in the Premier League last season. He grew under Unai Emery and scored when Villa beat Freiburg in the Europa League final in May.

It was one of Rogers’ less eye-catching goals: a clever jab at the near post from a low cross. There was a period last season when he could not stop scoring from long range but Rogers has spoken about wanting scruffier goals and he arrived at the far post to open his Chelsea account against Fulham.

Rogers is embracing the challenge. At Arsenal he would have been slotting into the finished article. Arsenal have reached the summit. Chelsea are beginning their climb under Alonso. Rogers, who has played in the Championship and had a loan in League One, rather liked the idea of starting lower down.

items.titleEn: Renée: “We’re going after the WSL”
items.summaryEn: Renée Slegers has made our intentions clear for 2026/27 - to win the Women’s Super League for the first time since 2018/19.
bodyEn: Renée Slegers has made our intentions clear for 2026/27 - to win the Women’s Super League for the first time since 2018/19.
The head coach sat down for her first pre-match press conference of the season on Friday ahead of our trip to Crawley to face Brighton.
She was asked what is exciting her most about the new campaign beginning on Sunday.

“The quality of players in the league, the quality of coaches, it’s all very exciting,” she said. “But I mainly look at what we have, what we’re doing and what we’ve done in the last six weeks - and the desire, quality and alignment we’ve created within our squad.
“That’s what I’m really excited to see, that’s all good, all nice and that’s a great foundation, but now let’s go and play competitive games.

“I think we’ve been open with it, it’s something we’re going after - and of course we are, because we’re Arsenal. That’s something we should definitely have as a goal - definitely the WSL, as I think 2018/19 was the last time for Arsenal.

“There’s a real hunger - of course, there are other competitions - the draw for the Champions League was today as well, and there’s the FA Cup. Those competitions are very important for us as well, but the WSL is something because of the two teams coming in, and there are more games, and it’s symbolic for endurance and consistency. It’s something we really have our mind set on.”
So what did we learn from last season’s encounters against the Seagulls, in which we won 1-0 at home, lost 2-0 in the FA Cup, and drew 1-1 away?

“They're a stubborn team,” Renée said. “I think they're a good team. They know when to press and press aggressively and make spaces small quickly. But they also know how to be patient and make it really compact in front of their goal. So it's been hard games for us. We acknowledge that. We won the game at the Emirates, but the other two weren't the results we wanted.

“So yeah, we look forward to the challenge and we know that there's things that they will make hard for us. And of course, there's a big belief in what we're doing at the moment, the quality that we possess and the different tools that we have to use on Sunday. So I really look forward to the game.

“Dario did a fantastic job with the team. So I wish him all the best. From what I understand, there's a couple of days that the new coach has spent with the team. I think what's been a trait of Brighton anyway is that they are unpredictable. Dario always had ideas against us, so we tried to prepare for things, but he would do something different anyway. So that's something we have to be really good at on Sunday as well, that we have to plan for certain scenarios, but also know that there might be things happening on the pitch that we haven't prepared for.
“And then we have principles that we can lean back on and we can problem-solve in the moment. But, yes, that's something that's been typical for our games against Brighton anyway.”
Lastly, the boss was asked what it will be like to see Lia Walti again this weekend, after the Swiss spent seven years in our midfield.

“Oh, yes, I look forward to it,” she said. “She... I had the time with her here at Arsenal and it was great working with her. I was mostly in the individual development role and I think we had some great collaboration. She's bright when it comes to football, when it comes to life, and I think it's really good that she's back in England and people can see her play in England again. So I look forward to seeing her, yeah.”

bodyEn: Renée Slegers was back in front of the media at the Sobha Realty Training Centre for her first pre-match press conference of the season.
Our head coach looked ahead to Sunday's trip to Crawley, where we'll face Brighton & Hove Albion to kick off the Women's Super League campaign.
Here's everything she had to say on the following subjects...

If we look at it, making big steps is never good - that’s always a risk. If you spike and load upwards or downwards, both are risks, so I think those steps need to be taken with a good rhythm. But also, we have such a big squad now, so we have opportunities to share minutes across the squad.

on the Champions League draw:I look forward to it - a draw is a draw, it’s not in our control. I’ve just seen it because we trained today and had a couple of meetings. on the latest team news:So our rehab players at the moment are Daphne van Domselaar, Katie Reid and Michelle Agyemang. And everyone else is fit to play.

on what qualities Élisa de Almeida will bring to the squad:I think she's competed at the highest level. She's been at PSG for five years now. She brings experience. She's good on the ball, which you have to be at Arsenal. She has a good athletic profile as well. So if you look at how our games usually play out, it's fast attacks and counterattacks that you have to manage really, really well. And she has the speed and the mobility to do that. So there's a couple of things within her profile that fit really well with the way we play.

on recruiting players within the 26-28 age category:Yeah, I think the work that's been going on in the background for a long time between Claire, Jodie, Kevin and the recruitment department, it's been so strong. So we've been planning for this window for a long time. And of course, age is part of what we look at as one of the factors. So really happy that we get players in their prime ages where we see they're at their prime, but there's more to come from these players. But also the younger ones that we were so happy we got them on board. They chose us. They want to be part of Arsenal as well. If you look at Isabella and Lisa, they're young, but they're so mature for their age. And I'm really, really impressed with where they are and the courage that they've shown, the humility that they've shown as well. So yeah, age plays a role in the decisions we make. And I think with all these coming in, I'm so happy with the strategy behind it.

So automatically, I think there's forward intent with these players. There's an athletic profile that we like with these players too. I definitely think with those players, they have what we want and need. Resilience, winning mindset, and just getting to work. Give me a task and I'm going to do it and I'm going to do it the best I can. So that's definitely things that they've brought. So I look forward to seeing her, yeah.

on if teams have to be less nice to win the WSL:Let's have a cup of coffee! No, it's interesting, because we are proud of the way we want to do things and that's our way. But finding ways and getting things over the line, for example, Crawley on Sunday, how are we going to get that over the line? And it doesn't always have to be perfect and exactly the way we thought it was going to be. But I think we've been in that with the group for a while now. This is the third year, I think, since we've been talking about that and I see growth from that perspective. And there's big buy-in towards that as well and understanding and a lot of learnings that we've gone through as a group together as well. So we do want to find ways and I think we will find ways this season as well in different scenarios.

on if we’ve got the players to turn draws into wins:Yeah, absolutely. The quality of players that we have here now and the variety. There's so many things that we can bring to a game now. It's so good. I'm so happy with it. So when I talk about Brighton and unpredictability, we want to be unpredictable as well with what we do, what the game plan is and what personnel we have on the pitch. So I do think we have the tools this year.

on if we’ve spoken about our previous slow starts in the WSL:Yeah, we've spoken about it with the staff, the captains, the player group and everyone is aware of it. And then from there on, it's important that we are in the moment, that we do everything we can in the moment towards our season ambition. But also think, start with the undermined. So what do we want to achieve? And that's what we're working towards and we know the hurdles we had last year. So there's strong awareness and I think that the schedule that we have is good. It's good for us, yeah.

on the value of getting lots of transfer business done early in the window:Really good. I think, like I said, we were very strategic about it. That's why we could do things early. And I think how it all fell together and what the squad looks like, it's really, really good. So it's really positive. I'm happy about it. And I think we've made late decisions, we've made early decisions and we knew how that was going to all come together. To have the full player group, that's why it was important for us this window, there was no tournament, so we had a full pre-season with the group. To then have those things ready early so we can start with the full group, apart from Elisa who came in yesterday, it's given us a really good foundation because there was a couple of things we were going after and to do that all together and the investment that everyone has shown in that process, it's been really good for us.
on if this is the strongest squad she’s had at Arsenal:Yeah, I would say so.

on how to prioritise competitions during a difficult schedule:Of course we look at the schedule and we see how is this, how we're going to prepare everyone and everything for what's coming ahead of us. Part of it is of course what we've done in the window, that we have so many good players that can play for us when the short turnarounds come and when we see necessary. Of course we prepare for the opposition that we're going to face. There's a lot of preparation, we have our ideas, but then it's still when the moments are there, we have to see how everything is playing out in the moment. So there's still a lot of, of course, late decision making in those short turnarounds as well.

on if she’s ever played against the new Brighton manager:No, I don't know him yet. I look forward to meeting him and it's interesting to get new ideas to the league as well. Everything I heard is really positive. I spoke to a couple of the Spanish players, so I welcome him to the English league.

items.titleEn: Arteta on Alonso, Chelsea and loving his players
items.summaryEn: Mikel Arteta has spoken about his relationship with new Chelsea boss Xabi Alonso
bodyEn: Mikel Arteta declared that he loves his players following the closure of the transfer window and ahead of taking on Chelsea this weekend.
We made five permanent signings this summer, including Piero Hincapie on a permanent deal, Illan Meslier, Christos Tzolis, Bruno Guimaraes and Ezri Konsa.
All focus is now on the pitch as we get ready to take on Chelsea on Sunday at Emirates Stadium and Mikel is fully invested in his squad.
"I love my players," Mikel said. "That's what I can say. I think at the end of the season we'll put everybody in their place and let's trust them.
"Let's make sure that we are right behind them and we do everything we can to help the incredible talent that they have."
The Blues are the visitors on Sunday, with Xabi Alonso in the opposite dugout, a man Mikel knows well.
The pair grew up in the same town, as well as both living on Merseyside when playing for Liverpool and Everton respectively.
Speaking about his relationship with Alonso, he said: "I spoke to him before [he joined Chelsea]. But yes, really happy for him, as I said.

"It's incredible because obviously we have the history that we have together, the same with Andoni [Iraola] and to be facing each other in such a level and with the responsibility we have managing some of the top clubs in the country is a really beautiful thing to experience.
"Our relationship goes on for many, many years and we share some great moments together. That's natural, but now it's the competition and when you face each other you know what happens."
One player who departed this week is Gabriel Martinelli after seven years in N5 and Mikel paid tribute to his contribution.

He said: "It's been a pleasure to work with him, to be part of this journey with him. The Gabi that I met and the Gabi that just left, it's a huge transformation, both in the personal side and in the professional side.

"I think the impact that he had for the club, his ambition, his love for the game and the way he has, I think, helped us to grow and achieve our goals. I think he's been a critical player. The story ends and we wish him all the very best in a different one. This is part of football."

items.titleEn: Arteta delivers update on Timber, Mosquera and Saliba
items.summaryEn: The boss shapes his squad ahead of our clash with Chelsea
bodyEn: Mikel Arteta has delivered an update on the fitness of several Gunners, ahead of our Premier League clash with Chelsea on Sunday.
Our return to N5 comes off the back of back-to-back league victories over Coventry City and Aston Villa, and now comes the test of Xabi Alonso’s Blues in an all-London showdown at Emirates Stadium.
Bruno Guimaraes made his Premier League bow in an Arsenal shirt at Villa Park and despite suffering a knock, the boss said the midfield man is being monitored ahead of Sunday afternoon.
“[Bruno] had a knock against Villa in the previous game and he’s being assessed,” said Mikel. "Hopefully [Saturday], he will be okay for training.”
Alongside Bruno came the debut of Ezri Konsa against his former side, with the summer arrival replacing Cristhian Mosquera following an injury issue which forced off the young Spaniard.
“For Cristhian, it was more precaution than anything else, so we’ll have to see in the session [Saturday] how he feels,” explained the manager.
“Ezri is certainly available in the squad, so we’ll see when we make our selection.”

Remaining at the back, Mikel also commented during Friday afternoon’s press conference that Jurrien Timber’s recovery is in a “really good place”, as he participated in full training alongside his teammates.
William Saliba also continues his path to fitness and has been named in our UEFA Champions League squad, making him eligible for our upcoming league phase fixtures.

“Jurrien is in really good condition at the moment, he’s been a few weeks on the pitch and has been training with us, so he’s in a really good place. We will decide [on his involvement on Sunday] after training [on Saturday].
“We don’t really know the amount of weeks Wilo is going to be out because it’s about a healing process and everything is a bit different - we know we have to respect certain timings.
“The progression has been really positive in the last few weeks, but we need to wait and see how that one reacts when we start to put some load into it.”

items.titleEn: Every word from Arteta's pre-Chelsea presser
items.summaryEn: Read every word from Mikel's press conference before facing Chelsea
bodyEn: Mikel Arteta has been speaking with the press ahead of our London derby against Chelsea at Emirates Stadium.
During his press conference, Mikel gave a team news update, assessed our Sunday opponents and much more.
Read the full press conference below, with a video above:
on Bruno's fitness:He had a knock against Villa in the previous game and he’s being assessed. Hopefully, tomorrow he will be okay for training.
on if Mosquera is available:It was more precaution than anything else, so we’ll have to see in the session tomorrow how he feels.
on if Ezri Konsa could start:He’s certainly available in the squad, so we’ll see when we make our selection.
on Timber returning to training:He’s in really good condition at the moment, he’s been a few weeks on the pitch and has been training with us, so he’s in a really good place.
on his availability for Sunday:We will decide again tomorrow after training.

on Saliba's timeline:We don’t really know the amount of weeks he’s going to be out because it’s about a healing process and everything is a bit different - we know we have to respect certain timings. The progression has been really positive in the last few weeks, but we need to wait and see how that one reacts when we start to put some load into it.
on if it was easy to include him in the UCL squad:Yes it was, and we had the space to do it as well.

on if he's happy the transfer window is closed:It is what it is - we don’t decide! I think we all know we had to make a decision on when we wanted the window to be closed, and now that’s it, and now it’s crystal clear everybody’s squads and where everybody has to be.

on not doing certain transfer deals:I don’t know - I think every moment, every situation is different. Sometimes we need to react because something unexpected happens as well, and you need to be prepared for that, so I think every case is different.

on a clause in Nwaneri's contract to return in January:Let’s see. The focus now for Ethan is to go and play in an incredible club. The atmosphere, setup, with Champions League in front of him, and all the talent at Dortmund. Then we’ll see what happens.
on Nwaneri potentially facing us in the UCL:That possibility is now open, with different rules to the Premier League, so yes.
on 'banking' Chelsea's front line:Banking will be the responsibility, obviously a team responsibility, more than a defensive one.
on our attacking options:What I have to say is that I love the players that we have, that’s for sure.
on Saka's form:He’s been very reliable so far in the first two weeks, I don’t know how many weeks there are to go!

on speaking with Xabi Alonso before he joined Chelsea:I spoke to him before that. But yes, really happy for him, as I said. It's incredible because obviously we have the history that we have together, the same with Andoni [Iraola] and to be facing each other in such a level and with the responsibility we have managing some of the top clubs in the country is a really beautiful thing to experience.

on if he was surprised by Chelsea signing Emiliano Martinez:No. Obviously, I know Emi really well. So we had him here as a top goalkeeper. It's clear what he's going to bring to the team and I think it's a really smart decision.

on if we have world class attackers:I love my players, that's what I can say. In the bracket, how you want to put them, I don't know. I think at the end of the season we'll put everybody in their place and let's trust them. Let's make sure that we are right behind them and we do everything we can to help the incredible talent that they have.

on his friendship with Alonso:Now it would be tougher to meet because of the schedule that we both have. But of course that relationship goes on for many, many years and we share some great moments together. That's natural, but now it's the competition and when you face each other you know what happens.

on using our academy in the first team:It comes, I think, with the quality you have in the academy, and some days it’s just a generation that can fit in at the right moment. It's about timing as well, the needs that you have. And I think as a club we want to provide the opportunity to our academy players to shine and to be at the level that we believe they can be. And so far, obviously, they've been really, really good.
on keeping everyone aiming for victory:That's easy. I think the message was clear from day one. So if you think differently, I don't think you have to be here, you have to go somewhere else.
on Chelsea using 'rugby pads' in training:That's something that a lot of clubs use; we use those pads as well. Everybody uses those pads in circuits. I think that's something very, very common.

on Gabriel Martinelli's departure:With great gratitude, it's been a pleasure to work with him, to be part of this journey with him. The Gabi that I met and the Gabi that just left, it's a huge transformation, both in the personal side and in the professional side. I think the impact that he had for the club, his ambition, his love for the game and the way he has, I think, helped us to grow and achieve our goals. I think he's been a critical player. The story ends and we wish him all the very best in a different one. This is part of football.

on missing out on a winger:I don't know, these are just opinions. The window is closed and I prefer to look at all the incredible things that we have in this squad and not to spend any more time on the things that are not part of us right now. That's it and that's my main responsibility.

on how he thinks Chelsea will play:That would depend on a lot of factors and game state is a massive one, especially because the two games that they played, they scored very, very early and that changes the momentum and the shift of the game. But they are capable and he's capable of playing in various ways. That's been a really successful match so far.

on if he took inspiration from Alonso's success at Leverkusen:First of all, the courage. Obviously, we've known each other for so long, we have experienced different countries, different moments and just to go abroad and deliver what he has done, the same with Andoni as well, I think it's remarkable. It shows you that I think doing what you feel and how you feel it and being able to translate that to a club, to players, and ultimately achieve the goals that you want is possible, regardless of where you are born and where you're from.

on not signing a player from Chelsea for the first time since 2021:I need to make that reflection. There is an opportunity and obviously a need that the club or the team has and the opportunity comes and this can happen. It's a good stat!

on whether we ticked the boxes in the transfer window:Yeah, 100% ticked. The outcome after can be different to what you expect, but the intention is certainly there, which is, in my opinion, what I value the most.

on whether there's a risk with the number of our attackers:I understand the point of view as well, but we have to understand as well the amount of minutes that those players played and the ones that were injured last year, especially in the first six months, and the data shows something completely different. But it is what it is. It is what we have, and as I said before, we already have some very, very good players.

on any regrets from the window:No, the sale of players can come from different aspects as well. It's not always the same one, and that's part of the responsibility that we all have at the football club.
on if ambition in the market means intent:Well, yes, because it doesn't depend on you only.

on how hard it is to pull off a big transfer deal:I think Andrea [Berta] is better, or Josh [Kroenke], to talk about that because I'm not in those negotiations. They know much better than me, so I think these are questions that are related to the market and all the aspects that I think it's better that they speak about it.

on if the higher prices in the market is bad for the game:Well, I'm sure when this happens it's because there's been an analysis behind it that this is going to be sustainable and all the kind of resources will appear or the valuation of every player will be then much higher and it will be done in a sustainable way. But again, that's, I think, something for the Premier League and the owners to look at and evaluate.

on having the ability to change our midfield entirely at Villa Park:That was really useful, and we discussed that game by game and then on matchday as well in relation to what the needs of the team or the moment requires to bring different kind of profiles to help us to win football matches, and Monday, that's what I said, that it was a squad victory because everybody contributed and very specific qualities helped us to win the game at the end.

on the partnerships in the midfield:Yeah, there are multiple. I started to do combinations and you cannot finish doing them and that's the beauty of it because they all complement each other and because they all have the mindset to be able to play and occupy different spaces throughout the game and that's what we need from our midfield.

on seeing two wingers can play on the same side:This is a very random situation, not something as a game plan but the chaos of the game or certain actions within the game because of a previous moment can lead you to those two wingers to play closer to each other because even if you want to, the speed of the game doesn't allow you to make those movements because you're going to need time in order to bring players that are 60 metres apart closer together. So it has a lot to do with the dynamics and the opportunities that the game offers.

items.titleEn: Introducing our six Women's Champions League opponents
items.summaryEn: The draw for this season’s Women’s Champions League has provided us with six opponents, some of which we have plenty of history with as well as some new faces.
bodyEn: The draw for this season’s Women’s Champions League has provided us with six opponents, some of which we have plenty of history with as well as some new faces.
We’ll be facing sides from France, Spain, Portugal, Norway and Italy as we look to get back to the final. As the dust settles on the draw, here's our guide to our league phase opponents!
LYON
How they qualified: French championsBest European Cup performance: Winners (2010/11, 2011/12, 2015/16, 2016/17, 2017/18, 2018/19, 2019/20, 2021/22)Last season: Runners-up

Eight-time champions Lyon reached their 12th final last season, with competition appearance record-holder Wendie Renard having played in every one. They lost the Oslo showpiece to Barcelona – the former club of OL coach Jonatan Giráldez.
Head-to-head: P9 W3 D0 L6

Our first meeting with Lyon came away from home in April 2011’s semi-finals, when we lost 2-0 thanks to a brace from Lotta Schelin. Our first win over them came in October 2022 - a resounding 5-1 success at Groupama Stadium.
They’ve been a frequent opponent of ours in recent years. We knocked them out of 2024/25’s semi-finals, before they got revenge on us at the same stage last season.
BARCELONA
How they qualified: Holders, Spanish championsBest European Cup performance: Winners (2020/21, 2022/23, 2023/24, 2025/26)Last season: Winners

Last season Barcelona became the first club to reach the final for a sixth year running, beating Lyon 4-0 in Oslo to claim their fourth title. They face their first European season without the departed Alexia Putellas, who played at least once in the previous 14 campaigns since the team's 2012/13 debut.
Head-to-head: P6 W3 D0 L3

September 2012 saw us meet Barcelona for the first time and we put three past them without reply at Estadi Johan Cruyff, the goals coming from Jen Beattie, Jordan Nobbs and Katie Chapman. One week later, we beat them 4-0 at home.

Barcelona got the better of us twice in 2021, winning 4-1 and 4-0, but of course they were the opponent for arguably the greatest result of our club’s history, when we won 1-0 in the 2024/25 Champions League final.
BENFICA
How they qualified: Portuguese championsBest European Cup performance: Quarter-finals (2023/24)Last season: League phase

Benfica ended 16th in the league phase last year but they kept up their record of ending top in every domestic season they have played in since their 2018/19 foundation, securing their second Portuguese double.
Head-to-head: P1 W1 D0 L0
Our first ever game against Benfica took place away from home last season, when second-half strikes from Beth Mead and Alessia Russo secured a 2-0 win at Estadio da Luz.
PARIS FC
How they qualified: French runners-upBest European Cup performance: Semi-finals (2012/13, as Juvisy)Last season: Knockout phase play-offs

Last season Paris FC finished ahead of Paris Saint-Germain to claim France's second direct league phase berth for 2026/27. They reached the inaugural knockout phase play-offs in 2025/26, exiting to Real Madrid.
Head-to-head: P2 W1 D0 L1

We failed to qualify for the group stage of the Champions League in 2023/24 after Paris FC knocked us out of the first qualfying round in Linkoping, beating us 4-2 on penalties after the game ended 3-3 in extra-time.
We did play them in pre-season this year, winning 1-0 at Meadow Park thanks to Olivia Smith’s 91st-minute strike.
HB KOGE

How they qualified: Danish champions; 4-1 h vs Riga, 2-1 h vs Hearts, 2-1agg vs PSV (1-0 a, 1-1 h)Best European Cup performance: Group stage (2021/22)Last season: Women's Europa Cup second qualifying round
HB Koge previously reached the old group stage in the inaugural season of 2021/22 and completed their first Danish domestic double in 2025/26.
Head-to-head: P2 W2 D0 L0
We played HB Koge twice during the 2021/22 campaign, winning 5-1 away from home with Steph Catley, Nikita Parris, Caitlin Foord, Anna Patten and Jordan Nobbs all on the scoresheet.
Then, we won 3-0 at home, Vivianne Miedema, Lotte Wubben-Moy and Foord all among the goals.
INTER MILAN

How they qualified: Italian runners-up; 3-3agg, 5-4pens vs Wolfsburg (0-2 a, 3-1 aet h)Best European Cup performance: Second qualifying round third place (2025/26)Last season: Second qualifying round third place, Women's Europa Cup round of 16

Founded in 2018, Inter made their European debut last season, losing to Brann in their Champions League second qualifying round semi-final. This time they have qualified for the league phase after defeating two-time champions Wolfsburg on penalties despite losing the first leg 2-0, and having to equalise again late in extra time.
Head-to-head: P0 W0 D0 L0
This will be our first ever meeting with Inter Milan.

items.summaryEn: We have been drawn against six teams in the league phase of the 2026/27 Women's Champions League - find out which ones
bodyEn: We have been drawn against Lyon, Barcelona, Benfica, Paris FC, HB Koge and Inter Milan in the league phase of the 2026/27 Women's Champions League.
With each club playing three games at home and three away, we'll be hosting Lyon, Benfica and HB Koge. Meanwhile, we'll be travelling to Barcelona, Paris and Milan.
The exact dates for these fixtures will be confirmed in due course.
The league phase format will continue as it has over the past season, with each team playing six matches against six different teams, three at home and three away.

All teams' results are compiled into a league table, and the top four sides qualify automatically for the knockout stage, while teams finishing 5th to 12th will compete in a two-legged play-off to secure their path into the quarter-finals. The last six teams are eliminated.
Last season, we came fifth in the table, meaning we had to beat OH Leuven in the knockout phase play-offs before reaching the semi-finals, when we were knocked out by Lyon.
The league phase matches will take place on the following dates:MW1: September 22-23MW2: September 30 - October 1MW3: October 28-29MW4: November 10-11MW5: November 18-19MW6: December 16
Ticket information for all these matches will be announced shortly.

bodyEn: Florian Wirtz is easing himself into his second season at Liverpool after a forgettable first. There were signs of promise against Nottingham Forest, where he set up the second equaliser and would have had a goal of his own if not for an offside in the buildup. It is clear the German needs to become more influential as a No 10 given the quality of players he has around him, especially after the expensive arrival of Bradley Barcola this week. Bruno Fernandes showed there is plenty of fun for an attacking midfielder to have against Ipswich and Wirtz can follow suit as a protagonist. Liverpool have drawn both their opening fixtures 2-2 and need something to kickstart their campaign, with a Friday night visit to promoted opposition a fine place to do so. Wirtz should cause problems but, if he does not, the internal competition will be after his spot. Will Unwin
Ipswich v Liverpool (Friday 8pm, all times BST)

Verticality, intensity and hard pressing are likely to be the order of the day at St James’ Park, where two German graduates of the Red Bull stable meet on Saturday at lunchtime. Newcastle’s new manager, Matthias Jaissle, is a former head coach of Red Bull Salzburg, while Bournemouth’s Marco Rose has managed Salzburg and RB Leipzig. “We have the same idea of how we want to play football,” said Jaissle – and Rose knows what to expect from Eddie Howe’s successor. “Matthias and me were several years in the style of Red Bull,” he said. “Everyone knows how we work. You can see it clearly. He’s a good coach. He’s brought his ideas really quickly into the Newcastle team. They are playing quite intense, they have clear pressing patterns that are different from before.” Louise Taylor
Newcastle v Bournemouth (Saturday 12.30pm)

Saturday’s meeting between two of the Premier League’s best-run clubs, Brentford and Sunderland, promises to one of the best contests of the weekend, with both sides physical, technical and superbly coached. Brentford, in particular, have made a terrific start to the season, the left side of their team looking especially dangerous. Keane Lewis-Potter provides impetus from full-back, with Mamadou Sangaré backing up strong ball-winning and carrying with intelligent passing, while Kevin Schade offers a threat in behind and, increasingly, in front of goal. All of which suggests a difficult afternoon for Thomas Meunier, Sunderland’s likely right-back who, at 34, has plenty of experience but might struggle with the athletic questions asked of him. He will, though, be able to rely on assistance from Noah Sadiki, whose nous, work ethic and running power will be invaluable in defending Sunderland’s right flank. How that battle plays out will go a long way towards deciding the game. Daniel Harris
Brentford v Sunderland (Saturday 3pm)

We can be sure any player Brighton buy has delivered the data metrics employed by the owner, Tony Bloom. But Chema Andrés, the 21-year-old midfielder just signed from Stuttgart, also nails the eye test. He was signed for £18.9m and it’s already tempting to speculate how sizeable the mark-up will be when Brighton sell him on. If we remember we’re talking about a sport, it’s impossible not to be excited about what the former Real Madrid academy midfielder brings to Fabian Hürzeler’s team. A No 6 of the old school, Chema offers economical movement but extravagant intelligence, evident in his passing and anticipation. Even if this weekend’s game against Leeds comes too early for him to be handed a start, he will make an impact soon enough. DH
Brighton v Leeds (Saturday 3pm)

It’s been a tricky summer for Crystal Palace despite their Conference League win. Oliver Glasner has gone, with two key defenders in Daniel Muñoz and Maxence Lacroix also departing and Jean-Philippe Mateta and Ismaïla Sarr trying their best to do likewise. This upheaval has left Pierre Sage, whose existing relationship with Malick Fofana wasn’t enough to secure the Lyon winger’s signature, with major problems. The former Lens coach is seeking to replace the club’s most successful manager while learning what works in a new league, with new players and without three mainstays. It wasn’t especially surprising to see Palace lose their first two matches, while Fulham have also been beaten twice while seeking to bed in a new coach and arrivals. More troubling for both teams is that the promoted sides look competitive. Hull and Ipswich have performed well and won games, while Coventry are better than they’ve shown so far. Though it’s far too early to talk about relegation, this already feels like a game of significance for two sides struggling for momentum. DH
Fulham v Crystal Palace (Saturday 3pm)

Manchester City spent more than £300m on new midfielders in this transfer window, but look light in the No 6 role, with Rodri and Nico González both departing. Ayyoub Bouaddi, bought as Rodri’s long-term successor, is only 18, so Enzo Maresca’s plan is to ease him into first-team action. The Manchester City manager deployed Marc Guéhi in a holding midfield role against Bournemouth, and is also confident Nico O’Reilly can switch from left-back to operate there. O’Reilly may line up at the base of midfield for Coventry’s visit, with City seeking a third straight win. Maresca is also not fazed by Omar Marmoush’s departure on an initial loan to Spurs, with Iliman Ndiaye arriving on deadline day and Antoine Semenyo also an able deputy centre-forward if Erling Haaland is unavailable. Jamie Jackson
Manchester City v Coventry (Saturday 3pm)

Liam Delap came off the bench against Liverpool and helped create Nottingham Forest’s second goal with quick thinking from a throw-in. The striker cost £45m from Chelsea but missed out on an intense pre-season after Xabi Alonso decided he was surplus to requirements, so needs to build fitness. Considering Tottenham’s major flaws thus far, it would make sense for Delap to be given the chance to spearhead the Forest attack. The former England Under-21s striker is the ideal No 9, quick, strong and a capable finisher, but needs to get all these attributes sharpened up. An outing against fragile opposition could speed up the process. Tottenham are bottom of the league having conceded five and scored none in two games, and compared with Chris Wood or Igor Jesus, Delap is a far scarier foe, as Oliver Glasner will know. WU
Nottingham Forest v Tottenham (Saturday 3pm)

They may have nabbed two wins in as many games upon their return to the Premier League but Hull were still not happy with their squad, seven new players arriving in the final week of the window. That means the Tigers have made 19 signings since promotion, which is an impressive turnover in personnel. Sergej Jakirovic needs to decide whether to incorporate these potential upgrades into his starting XI as soon as possible or make them earn the shirts from those who have accumulated six points. No one has let down the head coach or the fans over 180 minutes, so it would be harsh to drop anyone but, equally, having spent so much money on acquisitions, it could be argued that the sooner they get on the pitch, the quicker they will gel. It is not an easy decision for Jakirovic to make but he values loyalty and will want to challenge the mentality of the new arrivals – no one will walk into the side he has built. WU
Hull v Aston Villa (Saturday 5.30pm)

There are parallels between Manchester United’s visit to Hill Dickinson Stadium and their 3-0 win at Goodison Park in 2023 in the sense they will face a furious Everton crowd, and for the second time in four seasons the anger will not be directed towards them. Three years ago it was the Premier League in Evertonians’ sights after the record 10-point deduction that had just been imposed on the club. This time it is Everton’s owners, The Friedkin Group, in the firing line after the club’s shambolic end to the transfer window. There will be no flag displays inside the stadium after the group responsible for organising them, the 1878s, withdrew their support and there are calls for a “not a pound in the ground” campaign in response to the owners making a profit on transfers while leaving David Moyes with a weaker squad. Everton have started the season positively on the pitch, but are now surrounded by problems of their owners’ making. Andy Hunter
Everton v Manchester United (Sunday 2pm)

You have to go back to the start of the 2021-22 season, when Arsenal had Rob Holding and Pablo Marí in central defence, for the last time Chelsea beat their north London rivals, a run of 11 matches in all competitions. But they came close to ending that sequence in the 1-1 draw at Stamford Bridge last season before things began to unravel for Enzo Maresca, and the Italian’s successor, Xabi Alonso, will head to the Emirates to face his old friend Mikel Arteta in a competitive match for the first time as a manager full of confidence after winning his opening two games. Chelsea’s new-look front three of Cole Palmer, João Pedro and Morgan Rogers can certainly cause Arsenal problems, although the question is whether a defence that has conceded five goals can keep out the champions. Ed Aarons
Arsenal v Chelsea (Sunday 4.30pm)

bodyEn: Arsenal have confirmed Gabriel Martinelli has joined the Saudi Arabian side Al-Hilal for £60m. It is understood the deal for Brazil forward includes a sell-on clause.

Martinelli, who joined Arsenal from Ituano in 2019, has fallen down the pecking order at the Emirates despite being part of the squad that won the Premier League title last season. His fee surpasses the previous record £40m received by Arsenal when they sold Alex Oxlade-Chamberlain to Liverpool in 2017.
In the Guardian app, tap the Profile settings button at the top right, then select Notifications. Turn on sport notifications.
If you already have the Guardian app, make sure you’re on the most recent version.
If you don't have the Guardian app, download it from the iOS App Store on iPhone or the Google Play store on Android by searching for 'The Guardian'.

Martinelli is believed to have signed a four-year contract worth about £17m a season. His move was widely expected after Arsenal agreed a deal last week and has gone through before the transfer window in Saudi Arabia closes on Sunday.

The 25-year-old joins his Brazil teammate Gabriel Jesus in leaving Arsenal this week, the striker having moved to Barcelona for £8.6m. The Premier League champions also sold Fábio Vieira to Hamburg on deadline day but decided against bringing in players.

Arsenal are believed to have received about £3m from Brook Norton-Cuffy’s £14m move from Genoa to Hull owing to a sell-on clause in the England Under-21 defender’s contract but missed out on about £7m when Folarin Balogun move to Everton collapsed.

Tottenham have omitted Richarlison from their Premier League squad, with the striker not a part of their plans for the season. They could have accommodated him for the first-half of the campaign because one of their 17 senior non-homegrown players – Xavi Simons – is out until March or April, according to the manager, Roberto Di Zerbi, with an anterior cruciate ligament injury.

Spurs made clear to Richarlison before the closure of the transfer window in England on Tuesday night that he would not be included so he could arrange a move. He was unable to do so, with one to his former club, Everton, not happening. He is the subject of firm interest from Trabzonspor in Turkey, where the window remains open until Friday night.

Richarlison posted a message on social media on Monday in which he said he would not allow anybody to decide his future for him. He talked about his commitment to Spurs; how “when everything here was falling apart and they needed me, I stayed and gave my life”.

bodyEn: When Mikel Arteta revealed before Arsenal’s win at Aston Villa that he had pleaded with the Premier League to introduce bigger matchday squads, the final 24 hours of the transfer window was not quite what he would have had in mind. A deadline day on which Manchester City matched the British record to sign Enzo Fernández from Chelsea for £125m came and went as Arsenal allowed Gabriel Jesus and Ethan Nwaneri to leave without bringing in replacements.

With Gabriel Martinelli joining Al-Hilal for £60m on Thursday, there are question marks about the depth of the champions’ squad, despite Arteta still having at least two options for each position. Eberechi Eze will provide competition on the left for the new boy Christos Tzolis, and the manager has a plethora of central midfielders at his disposal after the arrival of Bruno Guimarães from Newcastle, but there is not much room for manoeuvre should Arsenal experience injuries in attack like they have for the past two seasons.

Arteta had been clear after the Villa game when asked whether he hoped to bring in more players. “We know that the depth has to be really big when you are fighting for four competitions in the manner that we play as well, so we’re going to try to do that,” he said.

Yet none arrived as Arsenal passed up the opportunity to bring in Malick Fofana owing to what it is understood were Arteta’s doubts over whether the Belgium forward would improve the squad, with Sunderland eventually beating Crystal Palace to his signature in dramatic scenes. The fallout has prompted some Arsenal supporters to question the wisdom of spending most of the summer, after missing out on Morgan Rogers to Chelsea, chasing “dream” transfer targets such as Vinícius Júnior and Julián Alvarez, with the sporting director, Andrea Berta, most in the firing line.

The Italian’s arrival from Atlético Madrid in March 2025 was heralded as a coup by many. Berta’s decisiveness last summer enabled Arsenal to rack up a net spend of more than £250m – comfortably outstripping their rivals – on players such as Eze, Viktor Gyökeres and Martín Zubimendi.

This summer the Premier League champions were quick off the mark to replace Leandro Trossard with Tzolis, then added Guimarães, before buying Ezri Konsa to cover the long-term absence of William Saliba, but the lack of attacking reinforcements on deadline day was eye-catching.

Offloading Jesus, one of the club’s highest earners, saved wages, and Martinelli’s departure as the club’s record sale would reduce Arsenal’s net spend to £78m – less than Brentford’s – compared with £162m at City, who spent more than £300m recalibrating their midfield. Iliman Ndiaye, who joined City from Everton for £65m, was another player on Arsenal’s shortlist who they opted against.

There can be no questioning Kroenke Sports Entertainment’s commitment to the cause, Arsenal having the second-highest net spend over past five seasons at more than £680m. Yet it will not have escaped the attention of some fans that it was confirmed on deadline day that KSE will expand its sporting empire with the purchase of the Major League Baseball side the Los Angeles Angels, for a reported $4bn (£3bn). With an estimated value of $26bn, it is not as if it cannot afford that.

Even before Arsenal wrapped up their first title for 22 years in May, the co-chair Josh Kroenke promised that “there will be no standing still when the season ends”, and bringing in Premier League-ready players such as Konsa and Guimarães was a statement of intent. However, the inability to attract real star quality in attack is an issue considering the heavy burden on Bukayo Saka after a couple of injury-hit campaigns. Kenan Yildiz could have fitted the bill but Juventus were not interested in selling the Turkey forward, and Alvarez made plain he wanted only Barcelona.
The Guardian's daily football game, On the ball, is now live in the app for both iOS and Android. Can you identify the Premier League star from the clues?

Arsenal struggled to break teams down during the second half of last season and became heavily reliant on their set-piece prowess, although a rejuvenated Martin Ødegaard has started the campaign promisingly.

Martinelli has failed in recent seasons to replicate his form of the 2022-23 season, when he scored 15 Premier League goals, but his pace off the bench often caused problems for teams who were chasing the game. None of Arteta’s remaining options possess that commodity, though Tzolis showed before a difficult half at Villa that he has the ability to create and score goals.

Eze, who missed in the shootout that decided the Champions League final against Paris Saint-Germain after coming off the bench, replaced the Greece forward against Villa and played a key role in Saka’s winner. Even after his heroics against Tottenham last season, scoring five goals against the team who were gazumped for his signature, the England forward has not nailed down a starting spot in the most important games. Eze could end up being the biggest beneficiary of Arsenal’s transfer inactivity along with Max Dowman, the 16-year-old who has yet to make an appearance this season.
After a summer of transition among their rivals, Arteta is banking on continuity to stay ahead of the pack.

Villa have generated about £300m from the sales of nine players and brought in 10 at a cost of about £250m. Villa have lowered their wage bill and changed the profile of their squad. Zion Suzuki, Ibrahim Mbaye and Johan Manzambi, names on the lips of Villa’s rivals, are particularly exciting signings. Last summer there was concern Villa had gone stale and 12 months ago they ended up fretting on deadline day – Harvey Elliott and Jadon Sancho joined on loan – but there was no such chaos this time. The horizon looks infinitely brighter than in June, when the playoff winners sold two players for a combined £8.5m to avoid breaching English Football League spending rules and a near-certain six-point deduction. Hull, remember, spent last season under a two-window EFL transfer embargo. A lack of money or, maybe, a reluctance to spend unless the finance was generated by transfers. Manuel Ugarte’s long-term injury (preventing his sale) and Joshua Zirkzee’s reluctance to move were factors. bodyEn: Aston Villa completed the signings of Ibrahim Mbaye and Taylor Harwood-Bellis on deadline day, with Unai Emery confident that the club’s radical summer overhaul has left Villa in position to replicate their recent success. Villa, who have lost both of their Premier League games this campaign, have qualified for the Champions League in two of the past three seasons and won their first major trophy in 30 years after lifting the Europa League.

The £47m arrival of the 18-year-old winger Mbaye from Paris Saint-Germain and £25m deal for Harwood-Bellis from Southampton represented Villa’s ninth and 10th summer signings respectively. Villa had generated more than £300m from the sales of nine players, six of whom started the Europa League triumph in Istanbul in May: Morgan Rogers, Ollie Watkins, Ezri Konsa, Youri Tielemans, Lucas Digne and Emiliano Martínez all departed Villa Park in recent weeks, Rogers and Martinez joining Chelsea.

Watkins’s £50m exit to the Saudi Pro League club Al-Hilal, after rejecting Villa’s offer of a new contract, led to Villa signing Nicolas Jackson for an initial £47.5m that could rise to a club-record £65m. Earlier in the window, Villa signed Johan Manzambi for a club-record £52m from Freiburg but the Switzerland midfielder is yet to make his debut as he continues his recovery from a knee injury he sustained at the World Cup.

After the 1-0 home defeat by Arsenal on Monday, Emery struck an upbeat tone. “We are happy how we are closing the transfer window,” the Villa manager said. “We are not regretting anything and the players who are joining are players that should be enough to rebuild the team with the structure we want. I think we replaced the players as we planned.”

Zion Suzuki, a £30m arrival from Parma, made his Villa debut against Arsenal and Villa’s new No 1 accepts the task of replacing Martínez is a “good challenge”. “It was my priority to play games so that is why I made the decision and I played in Belgium for one year, in Parma for two years,” said the 24-year-old, who joined Villa after a move to PSG collapsed in the final stages.

“In the end I am here and playing for Villa. I just wanted to come here for this club. There are so many expectations. It is not easy to play after [Martínez] but I want to help the team and be like him.

“It was very important to play in Serie A for two years and now I am confident. I made good steps and now I am here to play for the club. I want to enjoy this moment and help the team. I am really looking forward to [playing in] the Champions League but before that I want a first Premier League win to get some momentum.”
Newcastle, meanwhile, concluded a “transformational” transfer window by securing the target that topped their shopping list in May with only hours of the transfer window remaining.

The £51m signing of the Belgium forward Matias Fernandez-Pardo from Lille on deadline day is regarded as a considerable coup and prompted boardroom celebration at the end of a turbulent summer. The 21-year-old is Newcastle’s eighth signing of a transfer window during which Eddie Howe was replaced as manager by Matthias Jaissle and three of the team’s biggest names – Anthony Gordon, Sandro Tonali and Bruno Guimarães – were sold for a total approaching £250m.

Ross Wilson, Newcastle’s sporting director, kept in frequent contact with Fernandez-Pardo’s advisers. “Matias is a strong example of how a transfer window can unfold with twists and turns along the way,” Wilson said. “Back in May he was our top target and we always remained engaged with him. Now at the end of the window he becomes our eighth addition to a refreshed Newcastle United and we are excited to welcome him.”

Fernandez-Pardo’s elusive movement and ability to operate as a No 10, a No 9 or wide-left attacker explains why Newcastle were prepared to stay patient for his signature. “A lot of hours went into this one,” Wilson said. “But we’re clear on our identity and Matias has speed, intensity and work rate in abundance. We believe in his profile a great deal. Our fans will enjoy him and I know he will also enjoy our amazing St James’ Park atmosphere.”

Jaissle seemed equally delighted to have reinforced his frontline with a versatile attacker. “We were all delighted when we knew we could complete this deal,” said the German, who has made three key signings in the £39m Amar Dedic, the £52m Nico González and now Fernandez-Pardo since arriving on Tyneside in early August. “Matias is a highly technical player with explosiveness in his game. He can score and assist, he has courage and the ability to take players on. We’re sure our supporters will enjoy watching him play.”

The Belgian said: “I’m really happy to be here and very proud to be at such a big club. I spoke to the head coach and he really showed me how much he wanted me to be here. In terms of my career progression it made complete sense to come; I didn’t hesitate at all. I can’t wait to start my wonderful adventure here.”
Nick Woltemade’s failure to fit into Jaissle’s high-intensity gameplans explains why the Germany forward, signed for £70m from Stuttgart last August, has joined Juventus on a year-long loan.

Elsewhere, Barcelona have confirmed that Gabriel Jesus has joined from Arsenal on a permanent basis for a fee that is thought to be €10m (£8.6m). The Brazil striker was in attendance for Barcelona’s 5-2 win against Rayo Vallecano on Monday night after a deal was struck over the weekend and he leaves north London as only the 12th player to win the Premier League title with two clubs, having also done so with Manchester City.
Harvey Elliott has also joined Valencia on loan from Liverpool while, across Merseyside, Beto has sealed a £15.5m move from Everton to Fiorentina.
Kevin Danso has joined Sunderland on a year-long loan from Tottenham that should lead to a formal £25m transfer for the Austria centre-half next summer.
Fulham have completed the signing of Manuel Ángel from Real Madrid, having already signed César Palacios and Gonzalo García from the Spanish giants.

items.titleEn: Arsenal trying to lure Julián Álvarez after agreeing deals to sell Martinelli and Jesus
items.summaryEn: Atlético say they will not allow Barcelona to buy Álvarez Jesus poised for Barça and Martinelli for Al-HilalArsenal are running out of time to persuade Julián Álvarez to join them from Atlético Madrid after agreeing to sell Gabriel Martinelli, Gabriel Jesus and Fábio Vieira in deals collectively worth more than £70m.Álvarez has his heart set on joining Barcelona despite Atlético’s insistence they will not sell to their La Liga rivals – he returned to training on Sunday after being left out of their squad for the win against Sevilla. Continue reading...
bodyEn: Arsenal are running out of time to persuade Julián Álvarez to join them from Atlético Madrid after agreeing to sell Gabriel Martinelli, Gabriel Jesus and Fábio Vieira in deals collectively worth more than £70m.

Álvarez has his heart set on joining Barcelona despite Atlético’s insistence they will not sell to their La Liga rivals – he returned to training on Sunday after being left out of their squad for the win against Sevilla.

Mikel Arteta, the Arsenal manager, is understood to have spoken last week to Álvarez in an effort to persuade the former Manchester City forward to return to the Premier League and to have been informed the Argentina international wants only Barcelona.
Asked directly about Álvarez after victory at Aston Villa on Monday, Arteta replied: “I don’t know. That’s for the people upstairs.”

But Arsenal’s manager did confirm they are seeking reinforcements. “We are trying to improve the squad and until tomorrow night we are going to do that,” he said. “I have been disconnected from the world for 24 hours because I think my energy and focus has to be on the match, but I will get back on it now.”

Barcelona have agreed an £8.6m deal to sign Jesus, who has entered the final year of his contract after falling down the pecking order behind Kai Havertz and Viktor Gyökeres. The 29-year-old Brazilian was at Camp Nou to watch the 5-2 win over Rayo Vallecano on Monday. The Barcelona manager, Hansi Flick, said: “He’s a top striker and of course for us very important, he can give us a lot of things and [I’m] very happy that he’s here.”
However, the Spanish champions would like to sign another attacker after selling Ferran Torres to Paris Saint-Germain and are said to have not given up on Álvarez.
The Guardian's daily football game, On the ball, is now live in the app for both iOS and Android. Can you identify the Premier League star from the clues?

Atlético have agreed a deal with Juventus for Jonathan David on an initial loan with an option to make the Canada forward’s move permanent next summer. But they are understood to be determined to keep Álvarez, who joined from City in 2024.

Arsenal remain hopeful that the 26‑year‑old could change his mind but are believed to be monitoring several other attacking options. Everton’s Iliman Ndiaye was among the players on their shortlist but Manchester City are in advanced talks over a £65m deal for the Senegal forward. Arsenal missed out on Morgan Rogers to Chelsea and failed in an ambitious attempt to sign Vinícius Júnior, the Brazil forward signing a contract extension at Real Madrid.

Martinelli, who scored six times in the Champions League last season but only once in the Premier League, was due to have his medical on Monday after being left out of Arsenal’s squad against Coventry on the opening weekend. items.titleZh: 阿森纳同意出售马丁内利和热苏斯后，试图吸引胡利安·阿尔瓦雷斯加盟
items.summaryZh: 阿森纳同意出售马丁内利、热苏斯和维埃拉，总价超7000万镑，但仍努力说服阿尔瓦雷斯加盟。
bodyZh: 阿森纳在同意以总价超过7000万英镑出售加布里埃尔·马丁内利、加布里埃尔·热苏斯和法比奥·维埃拉后，正试图说服胡利安·阿尔瓦雷斯从马德里竞技加盟，但时间所剩无几。
阿尔瓦雷斯一心想要加盟巴塞罗那，尽管马竞坚持不会将球员卖给西甲对手——他在周日回归训练，此前被排除在对阵塞维利亚获胜的大名单之外。
据悉，阿森纳主教练米克尔·阿尔特塔上周与阿尔瓦雷斯进行了交谈，试图说服这位前曼城前锋重返英超，但得到的回复是这位阿根廷国脚只想去巴塞罗那。
在周一客场击败阿斯顿维拉后，阿尔特塔被直接问及阿尔瓦雷斯时回答：“我不知道。这由高层决定。”
但阿森纳主帅确认球队正在寻求补强。“我们正在努力提升阵容，直到明天晚上之前都会这样做，”他说。“我24小时没有与外界联系，因为我觉得自己的精力和注意力必须放在比赛上，但现在我要重新投入到工作中。”
巴塞罗那已同意以860万英镑签下热苏斯，这位29岁的巴西前锋在落后于凯·哈弗茨和维克托·哲凯赖什之后，合同已进入最后一年。他周一在诺坎普观看了5-2战胜巴列卡诺的比赛。巴萨主帅汉斯·弗利克表示：“他是一名顶级前锋，对我们来说当然非常重要，他能给我们带来很多帮助，[我]很高兴他在这里。”
然而，在将费兰·托雷斯出售给巴黎圣日耳曼后，西甲冠军希望再签下一位攻击手，据称他们并未放弃引进阿尔瓦雷斯。
《卫报》的每日足球游戏“On the ball”现已在iOS和Android应用中上线。你能根据线索认出这位英超球星吗？
马德里竞技已与尤文图斯就乔纳森·大卫达成协议，先租借后买断，明年夏天可以选择将这位加拿大前锋的转会永久化。但据悉他们决心留住阿尔瓦雷斯，后者于2024年从曼城加盟。
阿森纳仍希望这位26岁的球员能改变主意，但据信他们正在关注其他几个进攻选项。埃弗顿的伊利曼·恩迪亚耶在他们候选名单上，但曼城正在就这位塞内加尔前锋进行6500万英镑的深入谈判。阿森纳错过了摩根·罗杰斯（切尔西），并在尝试签下维尼修斯·儒尼奥尔时失败，这位巴西边锋与皇马续约。

用《卫报》对足球世界的看法开启你的夜晚
